views.name: delivered_orders_cohort
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  order_id,
  order_delivered_customer_date AS delivery_date
FROM
  olist_orders
WHERE
  order_delivered_customer_date IS NOT NULL
  AND (substr(order_delivered_customer_date,1,4) = '2016'
       OR substr(order_delivered_customer_date,1,4) = '2017'
       OR substr(order_delivered_customer_date,1,4) = '2018')
views.description: Select orders whose delivery/delivered date is present and falls in the years 2016, 2017, or 2018. Keep the order identifier and the delivery date (full date/time) for downstream month/year extraction.

views.name: delivery_date_parts
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  d.order_id AS order_id,
  d.delivery_date AS delivery_date,
  CAST(strftime('%Y', d.delivery_date) AS INTEGER) AS delivery_year,
  CAST(strftime('%m', d.delivery_date) AS INTEGER) AS delivery_month_number
FROM delivered_orders_cohort d
views.description: Project calendar parts from each order's delivery_date: delivery_year and delivery_month_number (1-12). Cast/normalize month to integer and year to integer. Keep one row per order.

views.name: monthly_yearly_counts
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  ddp.delivery_month_number AS delivery_month_number,
  ddp.delivery_year AS delivery_year,
  COUNT(ddp.order_id) AS delivered_order_count
FROM delivery_date_parts ddp
GROUP BY
  ddp.delivery_year,
  ddp.delivery_month_number
views.description: Count delivered orders grouped by delivery_month_number and delivery_year. Produce one row per month-year combination that exists in the cohort with the count of orders delivered in that month-year.

views.name: months_pivoted_report
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  m.delivery_month_number AS delivery_month_number,
  m.delivery_month_number AS month_name_or_number,
  COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN m.delivery_year = 2016 THEN m.delivered_order_count END), 0) AS delivered_orders_2016,
  COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN m.delivery_year = 2017 THEN m.delivered_order_count END), 0) AS delivered_orders_2017,
  COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN m.delivery_year = 2018 THEN m.delivered_order_count END), 0) AS delivered_orders_2018
FROM
  monthly_yearly_counts AS m
GROUP BY
  m.delivery_month_number
views.description: Reshape/pivot the month-year counts into one row per calendar month (1..12) with separate columns for delivered_orders_2016, delivered_orders_2017, delivered_orders_2018. Ensure months with zero counts for a year appear with zero. Include month name or number and order rows January through December.

views.name: delivered_events_filtered_years
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  order_id,
  order_delivered_customer_date AS order_date,
  CAST(strftime('%Y', order_delivered_customer_date) AS INTEGER) AS year,
  CAST(strftime('%m', order_delivered_customer_date) AS INTEGER) AS month,
  1 AS delivered_orders_volume
FROM olist_orders
WHERE order_status = 'delivered'
  AND order_delivered_customer_date IS NOT NULL
  AND CAST(strftime('%Y', order_delivered_customer_date) AS INTEGER) IN (2016, 2017, 2018)
views.description: Select all records representing delivered orders within the calendar years 2016, 2017, and 2018. Keep the date (or year and month) and the delivered_orders_volume value for each record; exclude any non-delivered statuses.

views.name: monthly_delivered_volume
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  CAST(strftime('%Y', order_delivered_customer_date) AS INTEGER) AS year,
  CAST(strftime('%m', order_delivered_customer_date) AS INTEGER) AS month,
  COUNT(order_id) AS monthly_delivered_volume
FROM olist_orders
WHERE order_status = 'delivered'
  AND order_delivered_customer_date IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY year, month
views.description: Aggregate delivered orders volume to compute total delivered volume for each year-month combination (i.e., sum delivered_orders_volume per year and month).

views.name: annual_delivered_volume
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  CAST(strftime('%Y', o.order_delivered_customer_date) AS INTEGER) AS year,
  SUM(oi.price + oi.freight_value) AS annual_delivered_volume
FROM olist_orders o
JOIN olist_order_items oi USING(order_id)
WHERE o.order_status = 'delivered'
  AND o.order_delivered_customer_date IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY CAST(strftime('%Y', o.order_delivered_customer_date) AS INTEGER)
views.description: Aggregate delivered orders volume to compute total delivered volume per year by summing all delivered_orders_volume for each year (using the filtered records).

views.name: select_lowest_year_and_its_top_month
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  a.year AS year_with_lowest_annual_delivered_orders_volume,
  a.annual_delivered_volume AS lowest_annual_delivered_orders_volume,
  m.monthly_delivered_volume AS highest_monthly_delivered_orders_volume_in_that_year,
  m.month AS month_of_that_highest_monthly_volume,
  1 AS result_row
FROM annual_delivered_volume a
JOIN monthly_delivered_volume m
  ON m.year = a.year
WHERE a.year = (
    SELECT year FROM annual_delivered_volume
    WHERE annual_delivered_volume = (
        SELECT MIN(annual_delivered_volume) FROM annual_delivered_volume
    )
    ORDER BY year ASC
    LIMIT 1
)
AND m.monthly_delivered_volume = (
    SELECT MAX(monthly_delivered_volume)
    FROM monthly_delivered_volume md
    WHERE md.year = a.year
)
views.description: From annual_delivered_volume, identify the year(s) with the minimum annual_delivered_volume; if multiple years tie, choose the earliest year. Then, for that selected year, find the month with the maximum monthly_delivered_volume and return the year, the chosen year's annual total, that month's monthly total, and the month.

views.name: customer_orders_sel
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  o.order_id AS order_id,
  c.customer_unique_id AS customer_unique_id,
  o.order_status AS order_status,
  c.customer_city AS city,
  c.customer_state AS state,
  op.order_id || '-' || COALESCE(op.payment_sequential, 1) AS payment_id
FROM olist_orders o
JOIN olist_customers c
  ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id
LEFT JOIN olist_order_payments op
  ON o.order_id = op.order_id
views.description: Select orders and their core attributes (order id, customer_unique_id, order_status, city, state, and link to payments) restricted to rows representing orders (no aggregation). This is the per-order cohort that later allows counting delivered orders and joining payments.
counter_examples: Please identify the top three customers, based on their customer_unique_id, who have the highest number of delivered orders, and provide the average payment value, city, and state for each of these customers.

Among all cities with delivered orders, find the five cities whose summed payments are the lowest, then calculate the average of their total payments and the average of their total delivered order counts.

views.name: customer_payments_agg
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  c.customer_unique_id AS customer_unique_id,
  AVG(p.payment_value) AS avg_payment_value,
  COUNT(*) AS payment_count
FROM olist_order_payments p
JOIN olist_orders o ON o.order_id = p.order_id
JOIN olist_customers c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
GROUP BY c.customer_unique_id
views.description: Aggregate payment records per customer to compute average payment value. This relation groups payment records (either linked by payment->order or payment->customer depending on schema) to produce the per-customer average payment value and count of payment records.

views.name: customer_delivered_counts_join
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  c.customer_unique_id AS customer_unique_id,
  COALESCE(d.delivered_orders_count, 0) AS delivered_orders_count,
  p.avg_payment_value AS avg_payment_value,
  COALESCE(c.customer_city, co.city) AS city,
  COALESCE(c.customer_state, co.state) AS state
FROM (
  SELECT
    customer_unique_id,
    customer_city,
    customer_state
  FROM olist_customers
) c
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT
    o.customer_unique_id,
    COUNT(*) AS delivered_orders_count
  FROM customer_orders_sel o
  WHERE o.order_status = 'delivered'
  GROUP BY o.customer_unique_id
) d
  ON c.customer_unique_id = d.customer_unique_id
LEFT JOIN customer_payments_agg p
  ON c.customer_unique_id = p.customer_unique_id
LEFT JOIN (
  -- representative city/state from delivered orders if any exist (fallback source)
  SELECT
    customer_unique_id,
    MIN(city) AS city,
    MIN(state) AS state
  FROM customer_orders_sel
  WHERE order_status = 'delivered'
  GROUP BY customer_unique_id
) co
  ON c.customer_unique_id = co.customer_unique_id
views.description: Count delivered orders per customer by aggregating delivered_orders_filter, then join with customer_payments_agg and a representative city/state for the customer (chosen from their delivered orders or orders table). Produces one row per customer with delivered_orders_count, avg_payment_value, city, and state.

views.name: payments_per_order
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  order_id,
  payment_value AS payment_amount
FROM olist_order_payments
views.description: Select payment records and associate each payment amount with its corresponding order identifier (one row per payment).

views.name: city_level_measures
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  c.customer_city AS city,
  SUM(op.payment_value) AS total_payments,
  COUNT(DISTINCT o.order_id) AS delivered_order_count
FROM olist_customers c
JOIN olist_orders o
  ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
JOIN olist_order_payments op
  ON o.order_id = op.order_id
WHERE o.order_status = 'delivered'
GROUP BY c.customer_city
views.description: For each city, aggregate payments and count delivered orders by joining delivered orders to payments; produce total_payments (sum of payment_amount for orders in that city) and delivered_order_count (distinct delivered orders count) per city. Do not apply ordering or top-k here.

views.name: five_lowest_payment_cities_averages
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  clm.city AS selected_city,
  AVG(clm.total_payments) OVER () AS average_total_payments_across_selected_cities,
  AVG(clm.delivered_order_count) OVER () AS average_total_delivered_order_count_across_selected_cities
FROM olist_orders o
JOIN customer_orders_sel cos ON o.order_id = cos.order_id
JOIN customer_delivered_counts_join cdc ON cos.customer_unique_id = cdc.customer_unique_id
JOIN city_level_measures clm ON clm.city = cdc.city
GROUP BY clm.city
HAVING 1=1
views.description: Order cities by total_payments ascending, take the first five cities (lowest total_payments), and compute two scalars: the average of total_payments across those five cities and the average of delivered_order_count across those five cities.

views.name: delivered_order_items
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  oi.order_id,
  o.order_status,
  oi.order_item_id,
  oi.seller_id,
  c.customer_unique_id,
  oi.price,
  oi.freight_value,
  r.review_score
FROM olist_order_items AS oi
JOIN olist_orders AS o
  ON oi.order_id = o.order_id
LEFT JOIN olist_customers AS c
  ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id
LEFT JOIN olist_order_reviews AS r
  ON oi.order_id = r.order_id
WHERE o.order_status = 'delivered'
views.description: All order items that belong to orders with status 'delivered'; keep item-level financials, seller, order, customer and rating fields needed downstream.

views.name: seller_item_profit
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  doi.order_item_id AS order_item_id,
  doi.seller_id AS seller_id,
  doi.order_id AS order_id,
  doi.customer_unique_id AS customer_unique_id,
  (CAST(doi.price AS REAL) - CAST(doi.freight_value AS REAL)) AS profit,
  CASE WHEN CAST(COALESCE(doi.review_score, 0) AS INTEGER) = 5 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_5_star
FROM delivered_order_items AS doi
WHERE doi.order_status = 'delivered'
views.description: Compute per-item profit for each delivered order item as price minus freight_value and normalize/clean numeric fields and review_score.

views.name: seller_metrics_agg
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  s.seller_id AS seller_id,
  COUNT(DISTINCT s.customer_unique_id) AS distinct_customers,
  SUM(s.profit) AS total_profit,
  COUNT(DISTINCT s.order_id) AS distinct_orders,
  SUM(CASE WHEN s.is_5_star = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS five_star_count
FROM seller_item_profit s
GROUP BY s.seller_id
views.description: Aggregate delivered-item-level rows to seller-level metrics: distinct customer count, sum of profit, distinct order count, and count of 5-star ratings.

views.name: top_seller_per_category
views.body_sql:
SELECT 'max_total_profit' AS description,
       s.seller_id AS seller_id,
       sm.total_profit AS value
FROM seller_metrics_agg sm
JOIN olist_sellers s USING (seller_id)
WHERE sm.total_profit = (
    SELECT MAX(total_profit) FROM seller_metrics_agg
)
UNION ALL
SELECT 'max_distinct_customers' AS description,
       s.seller_id AS seller_id,
       sm.distinct_customers AS value
FROM seller_metrics_agg sm
JOIN olist_sellers s USING (seller_id)
WHERE sm.distinct_customers = (
    SELECT MAX(distinct_customers) FROM seller_metrics_agg
)
UNION ALL
SELECT 'max_distinct_orders' AS description,
       s.seller_id AS seller_id,
       sm.distinct_orders AS value
FROM seller_metrics_agg sm
JOIN olist_sellers s USING (seller_id)
WHERE sm.distinct_orders = (
    SELECT MAX(distinct_orders) FROM seller_metrics_agg
)
UNION ALL
SELECT 'max_five_star_count' AS description,
       s.seller_id AS seller_id,
       sm.five_star_count AS value
FROM seller_metrics_agg sm
JOIN olist_sellers s USING (seller_id)
WHERE sm.five_star_count = (
    SELECT MAX(five_star_count) FROM seller_metrics_agg
)
views.description: For each of the four metric categories, pick the single seller with the maximum metric value and label the row with the corresponding description.

views.name: payments_with_product_category
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  olist_order_payments.order_id || '-' || CAST(olist_order_payments.payment_sequential AS TEXT) AS payment_id,
  olist_order_payments.payment_type AS payment_method,
  olist_products.product_category_name AS product_category
FROM olist_order_payments
JOIN olist_order_items
  ON olist_order_payments.order_id = olist_order_items.order_id
JOIN olist_products
  ON olist_order_items.product_id = olist_products.product_id
WHERE olist_products.product_category_name IS NOT NULL
views.description: All individual payment records joined to the product(s) or order items that determine the product's category so each payment is associated with a product category. Keep only payments that can be linked to an existing category.

views.name: category_method_counts
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.product_category_name AS product_category,
  op.payment_type AS payment_method,
  COUNT(*) AS payments_count,
  p.product_id,
  op.order_id,
  op.payment_sequential
FROM olist_products p
JOIN olist_order_items oi ON oi.product_id = p.product_id
JOIN olist_order_payments op ON op.order_id = oi.order_id
GROUP BY
  p.product_category_name,
  op.payment_type,
  p.product_id,
  op.order_id,
  op.payment_sequential
views.description: Count of payments grouped by product category and payment method (number of payments using that method for that category).

views.name: category_top_method
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  cm.product_category                                       AS product_category,
  cm.payment_method                                         AS payment_method,
  cm.payments_count                                         AS payments_count
FROM (
  SELECT
    product_category,
    payment_method,
    payments_count,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY product_category ORDER BY payments_count DESC) AS rn
  FROM category_method_counts
) cm
WHERE cm.rn = 1
views.description: For each product category, choose the payment method with the highest payments_count. If ties exist, keep any one tied method per category.

views.name: category_top_method_with_average
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  c.product_category AS product_category,
  c.payment_method AS most_preferred_payment_method,
  c.payments_count AS payments_for_most_preferred_method,
  (SELECT AVG(payments_count) FROM category_top_method) AS average_of_these_payments
FROM category_top_method c
views.description: Combine the per-category chosen top payment-method rows and compute the average of their payments_count across all categories; also emit each category's chosen method and its payments_count alongside the overall average (average is a scalar repeated or returned separately as required).

views.name: payments_with_product_category_22
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.order_id || '-' || p.payment_sequential AS payment_id,
  p.payment_type AS payment_type_id,
  prod.product_category_name AS product_category_id
FROM olist_order_payments AS p
JOIN olist_order_items AS oi
  ON oi.order_id = p.order_id
JOIN olist_products AS prod
  ON prod.product_id = oi.product_id
views.description: Join payments to the product(s) on each payment (via order/order_lines or payment->order->order_lines) and map each payment to the product category(ies) involved so each row represents a single payment applied to a single product category. Keep one row per payment-category pairing so payments that cover multiple product categories appear multiple times.

views.name: payment_type_names
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  payment_type AS payment_type_id,
  CASE
    WHEN payment_type = 'credit_card' THEN 'credit_card'
    WHEN payment_type = 'debit_card' THEN 'debit_card'
    WHEN payment_type = 'boleto' THEN 'boleto'
    WHEN payment_type = 'voucher' THEN 'voucher'
    WHEN payment_type IS NULL OR TRIM(payment_type) = '' THEN 'unknown'
    ELSE payment_type
  END AS payment_type_name
FROM olist_order_payments
GROUP BY payment_type
views.description: Resolve canonical names or identifiers for payment types so each payment_type_id is associated with a readable payment_type_name.

views.name: category_payment_type_counts
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.product_category_name AS product_category_id,
  op.payment_type AS payment_type_id,
  COUNT(*) AS payments_count
FROM olist_order_payments op
JOIN olist_order_items oi
  ON op.order_id = oi.order_id
JOIN olist_products p
  ON oi.product_id = p.product_id
GROUP BY
  p.product_category_name,
  op.payment_type
views.description: Aggregate the joined payment-category rows to count how many payments of each payment type occur within each product category. One row per (product_category, payment_type) with the count of payments.

views.name: category_top_payment_type
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  cpc.product_category_id,
  cpc.payment_type_id,
  ptn.payment_type_name,
  cpc.payments_count
FROM category_payment_type_counts AS cpc
LEFT JOIN payment_type_names AS ptn
  ON cpc.payment_type_id = ptn.payment_type_id
views.description: For each product category, pick the payment type(s) with the highest payments_count (ties allowed). Attach the payment type name and produce one or more rows per category for its top payment-type(s). Do not apply the final top-3 category filter here.

views.name: geolocation_rows
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  rowid AS geolocation_id,
  geolocation_state,
  geolocation_city,
  geolocation_zip_code_prefix,
  geolocation_lat AS geolocation_lat_deg,
  geolocation_lng AS geolocation_lng_deg
FROM olist_geolocation
views.description: Select all rows from the geolocation source with the raw columns needed for ordering and distance calculation (ids, state, city, zip prefix, latitude and longitude in degrees). No additional filtering.

views.name: geolocation_radians
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  geolocation_id,
  geolocation_state,
  geolocation_city,
  geolocation_zip_code_prefix,
  RADIANS(geolocation_lat_deg) AS lat_rad,
  RADIANS(geolocation_lng_deg) AS lng_rad,
  geolocation_lat_deg,
  geolocation_lng_deg
FROM geolocation_rows
views.description: Normalize/convert lat/lng degrees to radians and project the columns needed for ordering and distance math. Keep one row per geolocation id.

views.name: ordered_geolocation_with_prev
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  g.geolocation_id,
  LAG(g.geolocation_id) OVER (ORDER BY g.geolocation_state ASC, g.geolocation_city ASC, g.geolocation_zip_code_prefix ASC, g.geolocation_lat_deg ASC, g.geolocation_lng_deg ASC) AS prev_geolocation_id,
  g.geolocation_state,
  g.geolocation_city,
  LAG(g.geolocation_state) OVER (ORDER BY g.geolocation_state ASC, g.geolocation_city ASC, g.geolocation_zip_code_prefix ASC, g.geolocation_lat_deg ASC, g.geolocation_lng_deg ASC) AS prev_geolocation_state,
  LAG(g.geolocation_city) OVER (ORDER BY g.geolocation_state ASC, g.geolocation_city ASC, g.geolocation_zip_code_prefix ASC, g.geolocation_lat_deg ASC, g.geolocation_lng_deg ASC) AS prev_geolocation_city,
  g.geolocation_zip_code_prefix,
  g.geolocation_lat_deg,
  g.geolocation_lng_deg,
  LAG(g.geolocation_zip_code_prefix) OVER (ORDER BY g.geolocation_state ASC, g.geolocation_city ASC, g.geolocation_zip_code_prefix ASC, g.geolocation_lat_deg ASC, g.geolocation_lng_deg ASC) AS prev_geolocation_zip_code_prefix,
  LAG(g.geolocation_lat_deg) OVER (ORDER BY g.geolocation_state ASC, g.geolocation_city ASC, g.geolocation_zip_code_prefix ASC, g.geolocation_lat_deg ASC, g.geolocation_lng_deg ASC) AS prev_geolocation_lat_deg,
  LAG(g.geolocation_lng_deg) OVER (ORDER BY g.geolocation_state ASC, g.geolocation_city ASC, g.geolocation_zip_code_prefix ASC, g.geolocation_lat_deg ASC, g.geolocation_lng_deg ASC) AS prev_geolocation_lng_deg,
  r.lat_rad,
  r.lng_rad,
  LAG(r.lat_rad) OVER (ORDER BY g.geolocation_state ASC, g.geolocation_city ASC, g.geolocation_zip_code_prefix ASC, g.geolocation_lat_deg ASC, g.geolocation_lng_deg ASC) AS prev_lat_rad,
  LAG(r.lng_rad) OVER (ORDER BY g.geolocation_state ASC, g.geolocation_city ASC, g.geolocation_zip_code_prefix ASC, g.geolocation_lat_deg ASC, g.geolocation_lng_deg ASC) AS prev_lng_rad
FROM geolocation_rows g
JOIN geolocation_radians r
  ON g.geolocation_id = r.geolocation_id
views.description: Order rows by state ASC, city ASC, zip prefix ASC, latitude ASC, longitude ASC and for each row produce the immediate predecessor's key and coordinate fields (using a lag/lead-style window). One row per current geolocation with its previous neighbor attached.

views.name: pairwise_distance_candidates
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  o.prev_geolocation_id,
  o.geolocation_id,
  o.prev_geolocation_state,
  o.prev_geolocation_city,
  o.geolocation_state,
  o.geolocation_city,
  o.prev_geolocation_zip_code_prefix,
  o.prev_geolocation_lat_deg,
  o.prev_geolocation_lng_deg,
  o.geolocation_zip_code_prefix,
  o.geolocation_lat_deg,
  o.geolocation_lng_deg,
  -- spherical law of cosines distance in km; guard for numeric stability using LEAST/GREATEST
  6371.0 * acos(
    -- ensure the argument to acos is within [-1,1]
    CASE
      WHEN ( (sin(o.prev_lat_rad) * sin(o.lat_rad)) + (cos(o.prev_lat_rad) * cos(o.lat_rad) * cos(o.lng_rad - o.prev_lng_rad)) ) > 1.0 THEN 1.0
      WHEN ( (sin(o.prev_lat_rad) * sin(o.lat_rad)) + (cos(o.prev_lat_rad) * cos(o.lat_rad) * cos(o.lng_rad - o.prev_lng_rad)) ) < -1.0 THEN -1.0
      ELSE (sin(o.prev_lat_rad) * sin(o.lat_rad)) + (cos(o.prev_lat_rad) * cos(o.lat_rad) * cos(o.lng_rad - o.prev_lng_rad))
    END
  ) AS distance_km
FROM ordered_geolocation_with_prev o
WHERE o.prev_geolocation_id IS NOT NULL
views.description: For each row that has an immediate predecessor, compute the great-circle distance (km) between the row and its predecessor using the Spherical Law of Cosines with Earth radius = 6371. Produce one row per adjacent-pair candidate containing both ids, their attributes, and the computed distance.
